candidate.answerReason: The isosceles triangle has base angles of \(70^\circ\). The two angles at B and C in triangle BOC sum to \(70^\circ\), leaving \(110^\circ\) at O.

methods.label: Track the angles at the base
methods.explanation:
Because \(AB=AC\), the base angles at \(B\) and \(C\) are equal. The triangle angle sum gives
\[
\angle ABC=\angle BCA
=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}{2}=70^\circ.
\]
Let \(\theta=\angle OBC=\angle OCA\). Since \(O\) lies inside the triangle, \(0<\theta<70^\circ\), and ray \(CO\) splits angle \(BCA\). Therefore
\[
\angle BCO=70^\circ-\theta.
\]
The angles at \(B\) and \(C\) in triangle \(BOC\) consequently sum to \(\theta+(70^\circ-\theta)=70^\circ\). Hence
\[
\angle BOC=180^\circ-70^\circ=\boxed{110^\circ},
\]
choice A.
